text:
Elias Lindholm has a knack this season for the goal that changes a game. He's 17th of 515 skaters in wins added by goals, ahead of plenty of bigger names, and he scored Boston's opener in the 4-1 win over Florida. He has 7 goals and 15 points in 18 games, three goals in his last four.

The finishing is hot. Seven goals on 4.65 expected means a 21% shooting rate against a usual range around 14%, and Boston has scored 6.9 more goals than its chances deserve with him on. Both numbers tend to drift back.

That matters more because last season was rough: Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level, with opponents generating more against him than against most forwards. This season the Bruins get 55% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, a healthier sign. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking gives him a signature worth watching: 23% of his setups go across the royal road, more than three times a typical forward. When that pass is working, so is he.
headline: Lindholm is scoring on the shots that matter
